The taxonomy of splitting strategies usefully distinguishes subject overlap, stimulus overlap, and overlapping fMRI windows. Evaluating jointly unseen subjects and stimuli is a worthwhile benchmark objective.

Experiments span two public datasets, two signal modalities, and two established models. Large differences under comparable training settings—for example, Table 2’s BLEU-4 scores of 15.49 versus 0.99 for subject versus task splitting—demonstrate substantial sensitivity to the evaluation protocol.

It can therefore add a training subject’s edge to a held-out stimulus, reintroducing text overlap. Algorithm 2, line 33, has the analogous missing subject restriction. These may be pseudocode errors, but corrected algorithms and actual split artifacts are necessary to substantiate the claimed contamination-free benchmark.

Section 4.4 treats improving validation loss or generation scores with additional training as evidence of contamination or overfitting; such improvement is not diagnostic. The EEG reconstruction curves do not distinguish the proposed leakage conditions. Holding out subjects and stimuli is appropriate for its stated target, but independent recordings from the same subject can legitimately support evaluation of a personalized decoder. Claims about prior methods should be scoped to their intended evaluation settings.
